Package com.oracle.database.selectai.agent

Interface Task

public interface Task
Contract for Select AI agent task lifecycle management and metadata access.

A task is a database-side resource managed by the DBMS_CLOUD_AI_AGENT PL/SQL package. Tasks define work that can be assigned to or coordinated by an agent team.

A Task instance can represent an existing database task or be configured for creation. The name-only SelectAIAgent.task(String) factory verifies that the task exists and loads its metadata and attributes before returning. SelectAIAgent.listTasks() also returns handles with loaded metadata and attributes. A handle configured for creation is obtained with SelectAIAgent.task(String, TaskAttributes, String, TaskStatus).

A creation-configured handle retains its supplied attributes, description, and status without querying the database. Only such a handle can call create(); after creation succeeds, it becomes database-backed. enable(), disable(), and drop(boolean) require an existing task and operate on the database-side resource. Existing tasks can update individual attributes with setAttribute(String, String) or multiple attributes with setAttributes(TaskAttributes); both operations reload the typed attributes after the database update succeeds.

Before creation, getStatus() and getTaskAttributes() return the configured values. For a database-backed handle, each call to either method queries the database. getStatus() does not change the description returned by getDescription(). The description is supplied or loaded when the handle is initialized; getDescription() does not query the database.

Names and required Java arguments are checked locally. Loading metadata and executing lifecycle operations require database access; the database checks privileges and validates task attributes when they are submitted.

For a complete runnable example, see CreateTaskSample source.

1.1.0

  • Method Details

    • create

      boolean create() throws SelectAIException
      Creates this creation-configured task in the database. For a runnable example, see CreateTaskSample source.
      Returns:
      true when the database creates the task
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - when this handle was loaded from an existing task
      SelectAIException - when the database rejects or cannot complete the operation

    • enable

      boolean enable() throws SelectAIException
      Enables this database-backed task. For a runnable example, see EnableTaskSample source.
      Returns:
      true when the database enables the task
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - when this task has not been created
      SelectAIException - when the database operation fails

    • disable

      boolean disable() throws SelectAIException
      Disables this database-backed task. For a runnable example, see DisableTaskSample source.
      Returns:
      true when the database disables the task
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - when this task has not been created
      SelectAIException - when the database operation fails

    • drop

      boolean drop(boolean force) throws SelectAIException
      Drops this database-backed task. When force is true, the operation may be retried after the handle has already been dropped; the database force-drop semantics determine the result. For a runnable example, see DropTaskSample source.
      Parameters:
      force - database force-drop option
      Returns:
      true when the drop completes
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - when force is false and this task has not been created
      SelectAIException - when the database operation fails

    • setAttribute

      boolean setAttribute(String attributeName, String attributeValue) throws SelectAIException

      Parameters:
      attributeName - database task attribute name
      attributeValue - string value, or null where supported
      Returns:
      true when the update succeeds
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when attributeName is null or blank
      IllegalStateException - when this task has not been created
      SelectAIException - when the database update fails

    • getTaskName

      String getTaskName()

    • getDescription

      String getDescription()
      Returns the description supplied or loaded when this handle was initialized. This method does not access the database and the value is not changed by getStatus(). For a runnable example, see LoadTaskSample source.
      Returns:
      supplied or loaded task description, or null when absent

    • getStatus

      TaskStatus getStatus() throws SelectAIException
      Returns the configured status before creation or the current database status for an existing task. A pending task with no configured status returns null. This method does not change the description. For a runnable example, see LoadTaskSample source.
      Returns:
      configured or current task status
      Throws:
      SelectAIException - when current task metadata cannot be fetched

    • getTaskAttributes

      TaskAttributes getTaskAttributes() throws SelectAIException
      Returns task attributes for this handle.

      For a database-backed task, this method reloads the attributes from the database on each call and therefore can fail if the resource was deleted. For a creation-configured task, it returns the configured attributes without querying the database. For a runnable example, see LoadTaskSample source.

      Returns:
      current task attributes for an existing task, or configured attributes for a task pending creation
      Throws:
      SelectAIException - when the task no longer exists or current attributes cannot be fetched
